# Toast

overlays · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a short notice that something happened: saved, sent, failed. It shows in a corner and
leaves by itself. For something the reader must answer, use a Dialog.

```ts
import { toast } from 'topclassui/toast'
```

```tsx
'use client'

export function SaveButton() {
  return (
    <Button onClick={() => { toast.add({ tone: 'success', title: 'Invitation sent', description: 'They get an email within the minute.' }) }}>
      Invite
    </Button>
  )
}
```

- **Nothing to mount.** `TopClassProvider` mounts the one viewport. Do not mount
  `ToastViewport` yourself.
- **Before the provider.** A `toast.add()` made before `TopClassProvider` listens, such as
  one in a page's mount effect, waits and shows once it does.
- **Outside React.** `toast` is four plain functions: `add`, `update`, `close` and
  `promise`. Call them from a click handler, a fetch callback or any browser module.
- **The table below** lists the options of `toast.add`, not props. Besides them it takes
  `title`, which is required (it names the toast for a screen reader), `description` and
  `action: { label, onClick }`.
- **Tone.** `neutral` by default, with no icon. `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `info`
  draw an icon, so the meaning never rests on colour alone. `primary` has no icon either.
- **Duration.** Clamped to 0 to 600000 ms. `0` stays until it is closed. Left out, the
  provider's applies (5000 unless `toast={{ duration }}` on `TopClassProvider`).
- **The action.** One button under the text. It does not close the toast: call
  `toast.close(id)` in `onClick`, with the id `add` returned. A long label wraps.
- **Update and close.** `toast.update(id, options)` changes only what it names.
  `toast.close(id)` closes one; `toast.close()` closes all.
- **Promise.** `toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` shows one toast: a
  spinner, then the success or the error icon and text. A string step is the title. It
  returns the promise, rejection included: catch it.
- **Placement, limit, duration.** On the provider: `toast={{ placement, limit, duration }}`.
  `bottom-end` by default: the bottom right in English, the bottom left in Arabic. The
  newest toast is the nearest the edge. Three show at once; the next appears when one closes.
- **The x.** Every toast ends with one, and nothing removes it: a swipe is a drag, and a
  drag needs a second way (WCAG 2.5.7). It stays on the screen while any of its toast shows, even a
  toast taller than the screen. A finger cannot scroll that toast, so keep the text short.
- **Swipe.** Toward the block edge, and toward the inline edge the toast sits at, closes it.
  A centered toast has no sideways swipe.
- **Keyboard.** F6 moves focus to the toasts. Tab goes to the toast, its action, its x, then
  back where you were. Escape closes the toast that holds focus. Closing the last one by
  keyboard returns focus where F6 found it.
- **Timers.** Paused while the pointer is over the toasts, while one holds focus, and while
  the window is in the background.
- **Priority.** `high` is read at once, as an alert. Keep it for what cannot wait.
- **Over a dialog.** A toast shows above a modal Dialog's scrim, its x takes the mouse, and
  a screen reader still reads it. Tab stays in the dialog; F6 reaches the toast.
- **An island.** An Arabic `TopClassProvider` inside an English page shows its toasts in the
  page's corner, in the page's direction and with its English labels: there is one
  viewport, the outermost provider's.
- **A short screen.** Toasts taller than the screen scroll inside the viewport, by wheel and
  by keyboard. A finger on a toast swipes it rather than scrolling; tap each x in turn.
- **A phone.** The viewport pads the notch or the home indicator at its edge. A phone
  reports them only to a page whose viewport meta has `viewport-fit=cover`.

### What Base UI gives

| What | How |
|---|---|
| The live region | `role="region"`, `aria-live="polite"`, named by `labels.toast.region` |
| F6 | Moves focus to the viewport; Tab past the last toast returns it |
| Pauses | On hover, on focus, and when the window loses focus |
| Priority | A hidden `role="alert"` copy of a `high` toast |
| The limit | `data-limited` on the toasts past it, which stay mounted, hidden |
| The swipe | Follows the finger; past 40 px in an allowed direction it closes |
| Promise | Writes the types `loading`, `success` and `error` itself |

### Not built

The collapsed stack that expands on hover (the toasts are a plain column), the entering
slide (a toast fades), anchored toasts (Base UI's `Toast.Positioner`), `pauseOnHover` and
`dismissible` as props (both are always on), and a queue for calls made before the
provider mounts.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { ToastViewport, toast } from 'topclassui/toast'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | no | `number`, min 0, max 600000 | - | toast.add: milliseconds before it closes itself, clamped; 0 stays until closed; left out, the provider duration applies. |
| `priority` | no | `low` \| `high` | `"low"` | toast.add: high is announced at once, as an alert; low waits for the reader to finish. |
| `tone` | no | `primary` \| `neutral` \| `success` \| `warning` \| `danger` \| `info` | `"neutral"` | toast.add: what the toast means. success, warning, danger and info draw an icon; neutral and primary none. |

Anything else on `ToastViewport` is passed to the element it draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
